title: Tom Slick: Not the Cartoon
summary:
Josh and an iHeart host (credited in transcript as "iHeart Intro", who is Chuck in the clip) profile Tom Slick Junior (1916–1962), a wealthy Oklahoma-born oilman's son turned scientist, philanthropist and cryptid hunter. Covers his father Tom Slick Senior, the 1933 Urschel kidnapping that involved Machine Gun Kelly, his Yale years and the Loch Ness trip, the Brangus cattle breed, his research institutes in San Antonio (including Southwest Research Institute and the Foundation for Applied Research), the lift slab construction method, possible CIA and spy work in South America and Tibet, the Dalai Lama's escape from Tibet, three Yeti expeditions in the Himalayas, the stolen Yeti thumb and the Pangboche temple story, Bigfoot hunting with Peter Byrn, his personal life, his death in a 1962 plane crash, and the fictional podcast Tom Slick: Mystery Hunter. The episode closes with a listener mail segment about the origin of the word sheriff."
  Note: the transcript spells the hunter's name Burn in places and Byrn elsewhere; the segments below use "Byrn" as in the hosts' later references to the brothers' surname.

segments.title: Opening banter and Tom Slick name confusion
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the episode, discuss the Tom Slick cartoon, and mention the fictional iHeart podcast about him, plus the difficulty of finding a full picture of his life.

segments.title: Early life and the Slick oil fortune
segments.summary: Tom Slick Senior, a wildcatter who struck the Wheeler No. 1 well, made the family rich. Junior was born in 1916, lost his father to a stroke at 46, and his mother later married her late husband's brother-in-law, Charles Urschel.

segments.title: Urschel kidnapping in 1933
segments.summary: Machine Gun Kelly kidnapped Charles Urschel and Walter Jarrett in July 1933 at the Slick family home in Oklahoma City, demanding ransom. Urschel gathered clues while held and was released after the ransom was paid. Kelly was later captured and sent to Alcatraz.

segments.title: Science interests and the Brangus cattle breed
segments.summary: Tom Slick studied genetics at Yale and pursued hybridization, including a failed attempt to breed a hog-goat. He created the Brangus cattle breed by crossing Brahman and Angus cattle, aiming to help hot climates rather than to profit.

segments.title: Cryptids, Loch Ness and early research institutes
segments.summary: Slick's love of cryptids came from his father. As a Yale student he drove to Scotland in 1937 to look for the Loch Ness Monster. He later founded Science City and several research facilities in San Antonio, three of which still operate.

segments.title: Navy service, South America and possible spying
segments.summary: Slick was turned down for combat due to eyesight and worked for the War Production Board and the Board of Economic Warfare in Santiago, Chile. Records of his Chile work were destroyed; the hosts say family lore and circumstantial evidence suggest he worked as a spy or in anti-Nazi operations.

segments.title: Philosophy of trying and the lift slab method
segments.summary: Slick said he did not believe in failure, only outcomes. The hosts describe his lift slab construction method, which lifted concrete floors into place hydraulically; Philip Utes developed it at the same time.

segments.title: Other inventions and unrealized projects
segments.summary: The hosts mention a mouse breed for chemotherapy testing, a claimed hair tonic for cowlicks, an institute's role in early oral contraceptives, and a failed plan for artificial pecans.

segments.title: Mysticism, India trip and the Dalai Lama's escape
segments.summary: Slick traveled to India in the 1950s, saw fire walking and reported levitating lamas, and later had a role in the story of the Dalai Lama leaving Tibet. The CIA ran a program in Tibet and helped the Dalai Lama establish a government in exile.

segments.title: Yeti expeditions and the Pangboche Yeti thumb
segments.summary: Slick led three Himalayan Yeti expeditions, the first in winter 1956 where he found a footprint. The second was a 1958 nine-month expedition with trackers and tranquilizer guns. The third, with Peter and Brian Byrn, involved stealing a Yeti thumb from Pangboche temple. It was smuggled out of India in his wife's underwear bag and turned out to be human, decades later per DNA testing in 2011.

segments.title: Yeti thumb aftermath and Bigfoot hunting
segments.summary: The Yeti scalp turned out to be from a Himalayan goat. Peter Byrn had a role in helping the CIA move people in and out of Tibet. The New York Times reported on the hunt in 1957. Slick later focused on Bigfoot hunting, and Peter Byrn continued it and wrote a book about it.

segments.title: Personal life, death and legacy
segments.summary: Slick married twice and had many girlfriends. He wrote two books on world peace. He died in a 1962 plane crash over Montana at age 46 and is buried in San Antonio. His research foundations later contributed to vaccines, the COVID vaccine, and other work, and his art collection is at the McNay Art Museum.

segments.title: Fictional Tom Slick podcast with Owen Wilson
segments.summary: Chad's scripted iHeart podcast Tom Slick: Mystery Hunter stars Owen Wilson as Slick and Sissy Spacek, with a voice part for the host. A short clip plays. The hosts note the show is highly fictionalized.

segments.title: Transition to listener mail
segments.summary: The hosts say where to find the podcast and move to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail: origin of the word sheriff
segments.summary: Listener Adam writes that the word sheriff comes from shire reeve, the county official, shortened to shereeve and then sheriff, citing a criminal justice professor.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts thank Adam, invite more listener facts, and sign off with the show credits.
